i0: We use the **past simple** for actions and situations that **finished** in the past: *I **watched** a film last night. We **went** to Spain in 2022.*
i1: Regular verbs add *-ed* (*work → worked*). Many common verbs are irregular (*go → went*). For the past of *be*, see [Was and Were](/blog/grammar/was-were/).
pst-regular.s: Add **-ed** to regular verbs: *work → worked, live → lived, study → studied, stop → stopped*. Same form for every person.
pst-regular.b0.0.2: work → work**ed**, want → want**ed**, play → play**ed**
pst-regular.b0.1.2: live → live**d**, like → like**d**, dance → dance**d**
pst-regular.b0.2.2: study → stud**ied**, try → tr**ied**, carry → carr**ied**
pst-regular.b0.4.2: stop → sto**pped**, plan → pla**nned**, drop → dro**pped**
pst-regular.b1: The form is the same for *I, you, he, she, it, we, they*: *I **worked**, she **worked**, they **worked**.*
pst-regular.b2: **Pronunciation.** After *t* or *d*, *-ed* is an extra syllable /ɪd/: *want**ed**, need**ed**, start**ed***. After other sounds it is just /t/ or /d/: *work**ed** (/t/), play**ed** (/d/)*. Don't say *work-ed*.
pst-irregular.s: Many common verbs have a special past form: *go → went, have → had, see → saw, buy → bought*. Learn them as words.
pst-irregular.b0: Irregular verbs don't add *-ed*. You need to learn their past forms. Here are some of the most common:
pst-irregular.b2: Like regular verbs, the past form is the same for every person: *I **went**, she **went**, they **went**.*
pst-irregular.b3: Some verbs don't change at all: *put → put, cut → cut, cost → cost, hit → hit, let → let*. *Read* is written the same but pronounced differently: *read* (/riːd/) → *read* (/red/).
pst-negative-questions.s: Negative: **didn't + base verb**. Question: **Did + subject + base verb?** *I didn't go. Did you go?*
pst-negative-questions.b1: After *didn't* and *did*, use the **base verb** (no *-ed*, no irregular past): *She **didn't go**.* Not *She didn't went*.
pst-negative-questions.b2: When *who* or *what* is the **subject**, don't use *did*: ***Who called** you?* (Someone called you.) Compare: *Who **did** you **call**?* (You called someone.)
pst-negative-questions.w2: Wh-question: where + did + subject + base verb.
pst-time-ago.t: Time words: yesterday, last week, ago, in 2010
pst-time-ago.s: Use the past simple with **finished** time: *yesterday, last Monday, two years ago, in 2010, when I was young*.
pst-time-ago.b0.0.1: *yesterday, yesterday morning, the day before yesterday*
pst-time-ago.b0.1.1: *last night, last week, last Monday, last year* (no *the*)
pst-time-ago.b0.2.1: *ten minutes ago, three days ago, a long time ago* (after the time)
pst-time-ago.b0.3.1: *in 2010, in May, on Friday, at 8 o'clock*
pst-time-ago.b0.4.1: *when I was a child, when we lived in Paris*
pst-time-ago.b1: ***Ago*** comes **after** the period of time: *I met her **two years ago**.* Not *before two years* or *ago two years*.
pst-time-ago.b2: Say ***last night***, not *yesterday night*. Say ***last week***, not *the last week* (*the last week* means the seven days up to now).
pst-time-ago.b3: Questions about finished time use *When…?* + past simple: ***When did** you **arrive**?* Not *When have you arrived?* See [Present Perfect vs Past Simple](/blog/grammar/present-perfect-vs-past-simple/).
pst-sequence.t: Telling a story: events in order
pst-sequence.s: Use the past simple for a series of finished events, one after another: *I got up, had a shower and left.*
pst-sequence.b0: When we tell what happened, one action after another, we use the past simple for each action: *She **opened** the door, **looked** around and **walked** in.*
pst-sequence.b1: Useful sequence words: *first, then, after that, next, later, finally, in the end.*
pst-sequence.b2: The past simple is also used for **past habits** and for **finished periods**: *I **walked** to school every day. She **worked** there for ten years* (she doesn't now).
pst-sequence.b3: Don't change tense in the middle of a story without a reason: *I went in and **sat** down.* Not *I went in and sit down.*
pst-tricky-verbs.t: Irregular verbs that are easy to mix up
pst-tricky-verbs.s: Some past forms look or sound similar: *fell / felt, thought / taught, bought / brought, left / lived, won / earned*.
pst-tricky-verbs.b1: These pairs cause many mistakes in writing and speaking: *I **fell** off my bike* (fall) is different from *I **felt** ill* (feel).
pst-tricky-verbs.b2: *Bought* (buy) and *brought* (bring) sound almost the same. *Brought* has an **r**, like *bring*: *I **brought** a cake to the party* (I carried it there). *I **bought** a cake* (I paid for it).
x.pst-sequence-s02: The period is finished (he retired): past simple.
x.pst-sequence-s03: Next event in the story: past simple.
q.pst-regular-b02: Which is the past simple of *plan*?
q.pst-regular-b03: In which verb is *-ed* pronounced as an extra syllable /ɪd/?
x.pst-regular-b03: After *t* or *d* we add a syllable: *want-ed*.
x.pst-regular-b07: One vowel + one consonant: double the *p*.
x.pst-sequence-b01: Past simple for the next event.
x.pst-sequence-b02: Sequence in the past: past simple.
x.pst-sequence-b03: Past habit: past simple (or *used to go*).
q.pst-sequence-b04: Which sentence tells events in order correctly?
x.pst-sequence-b04: All three events are in the past simple.
